text:
maria.chen: Heads up — canary A/B showing a perf regression after the merge of PR#3456. 95th latency up ~18% on long tails.
ajay: I can reproduce on the canary cluster. KV miss rate jumped ~3x for short context traffic. traces look like KV eviction churn.
leo: I started a quick bisect — current suspect is the kernel-selector change in runtime/kernel-selector.c from PR#3456. It changed heuristics for small-batch vs. low-latency paths.
sophia: CI perf job also flagged this earlier this morning: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/4267 — perf/regression test 95th +17%
ci-bot: Performance check failed: 95th_latency increased by 17.8% vs baseline. Test: canary-tail-latency. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/4267
maria.chen: Ops watchdog already paused the rollout: "SLO-WATCHDOG: Pause canary group A" — looks like our automatic gate fired.
ops-bot: Auto-gate triggered: metric=95th_latency, threshold=+12%, action=PAUSE_CANARY, group=A
ajay: Quick question — is this KV miss due to new kernel picking different prefetch/batching kernels? Kernel-selector started preferring batch-friendly kernels even for single-sequence requests.
leo: Exactly. The new heuristic biases toward kernel X for reduced throughput variance, but it increases memory working set for short queries -> more KV churn.
sophia: Any easy mitigation we can flip in canary without full revert? Maybe force kernel fallback for canary or tweak batching hint.
maria.chen: Proposal: patch the rollout policy to force kernel_selector.mode=legacy for canary A, and allow canary to continue while we bisect further. Minimal config change.
ajay: I can push a short-lived gate config: 
```
route.canaryA.kernel_selector: legacy
route.canaryA.batch_hint: low_latency
```
Will validate on staging and then update canary via console API.
leo: Meanwhile I’ll continue bisecting to identify the exact commit in PR#3456 that introduced the adverse heuristic. If we can narrow to a single function change we can hotfix instead of reverting.
sophia: Note: reverting the entire PR will lose some batching improvements for other workloads. Prefer config toggle if possible.
ci-bot: New perf job queued with kernel_selector=legacy on canary A: https://ci.internal/jobs/4272
maria.chen: If the canary resumes with legacy kernel and perf returns to baseline we can roll forward with a guard: add automatic kernel fallback when kv_miss_rate > 1.5x and 95th > threshold.
ajay: I can add that fallback in routing policy: fallback_rule: if (kv_miss_rate > 1.5 && latency95 > 1.12*base) => kernel_selector=legacy
leo: Sounds good. Also let's add a short-circuit in runtime to avoid aggressive prefetch when sequence_len < 32 — should reduce working set.
sophia: I'll coordinate a postmortem note for release owners and flag the rollout blocker in the release board.
ops-bot: Action items summary: 1) ajay: push canary kernel override (in progress). 2) leo: continue bisect + PR hotfix candidate. 3) maria.chen: update rollout guard rule. 4) sophia: postmortem + release flagging.
maria.chen: Thanks all. Keep replies short — we want to unpause only after CI with legacy kernel passes and 95th back to baseline.
ajay: pushing config now, will report results in ~10m.
ci-bot: Job 4272 finished: 95th_latency change = +1.2% (within threshold). Artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/4272
maria.chen: Looks safe to resume canary A with override. Leaving gate in place until leo's bisect completes.
leo: Found the offending change: kernel-selector heuristic in decide_kernel_for_seq() — patch ready (link to branch) with additional guard on seq_len and kv_estimate.
sophia: Great. After patch lands we should remove the override and monitor 24h. I'll schedule canary re-evaluation window.
maria.chen: Marking this thread resolved when patch is merged and rolling metrics stable for 24h. :white_check_mark:
